Nabe.et: From Middle High German nabe, from Old High German naba, from Proto-West Germanic *nabu, from Proto-Germanic *nabō (“nave”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₃nebʰ- (“nave, hub”).

Nabel.et: From Middle High German nabel, nabele, from Old High German nabalo, from Proto-West Germanic *nabulō, from Proto-Germanic *nabalô, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₃nóbʰōl.

Nabelschnur.et: 18th century, from Nabel (“navel”) + Schnur (“cord, string”). In Old and Middle High German, the word for “navel” was used in this sense on its own, though it is possible that similar compounds were already formed on occasion.

Näber.et: From Old High German nabagēr, from Proto-Germanic *nabōgaizaz. Cognate with English auger, Dutch avegaar.

Naber.et: In most cases from Middle Low German nâber (“neighbour”).
